hints: Look at the arrow direction on the curved lines joining P and Q - do they point away from P toward Q or toward P away from Q?
Recall that electric field direction is the force on a positive test charge, so lines leave a positive charge and enter a negative charge.
Compare how many field lines start or end at P with how many start or end at Q, since number of lines is proportional to magnitude of charge.
walkthrough: Identify the direction of the field lines between the charges: the central and curved lines have arrows pointing from P on the left to Q on the right.
Apply the rule for field direction: $E$ is in the direction of the force on a positive test charge, so lines leave a positive charge and enter a negative charge.
Conclude polarity: since lines leave P and enter Q, P must be positively charged and Q must be negatively charged.
Compare charge magnitude using line density: many more lines radiate from P than converge on Q, and some lines from P go to infinity.
Recall that number of field lines $N$ is proportional to $|Q|$, so more lines at P means $|P| > |Q|$.
Combine polarity and magnitude: P is positive with greater charge than Q. This is option D.

options.A: P cannot be negative because field lines leave P and enter Q, and P cannot be smaller because more lines connect to P than to Q.
options.B: P cannot be negative because the arrows between P and Q point away from P toward Q, which shows P is the source of the field.
options.C: P is positive but it cannot be smaller than Q because the much larger number of field lines at P shows a larger magnitude of charge.
options.D: Field lines leave P and enter Q so P is positive and Q is negative, and the greater density of lines at P shows $|P| > |Q|$.
